files.line: Point your phone at any car — and know what it is, what it's worth, and what to do next.
Meet the garage. One photo names the car. A VIN photo fills in the blanks. One tap registers it — and the app never guesses a field it cannot see.
It knows what I know. That engine computer has no EWS, the E30 crowd wants it, two hundred bucks. I taught it that. It doesn't guess.
Beside every rule grade sits a money grade, priced from real sold ranges — with the sold count and the reliability right on the card.
Nothing posts without my tap. The draft waits for me. That's the rule.
It builds the plan. Then a test fails, and it changes its mind — and shows you exactly why. That's not a chatbot. That's a tech thinking.
And it knows when to say no — before anyone wastes time.

Two engines, one verdict. The rules decide. The open model gets a second look — and it caught what the rules missed: my own notes. It read 'roadside spare, keep, don't list' and said don't list. That's a second look worth having.
